title: 1.5.31 A1.5.1 Part 2 — Implement Your Plan
description: Turn the chart you just passed into working JavaScript, and confirm the code matches the plan. Auto-graded.

steps.title: Write the plan down first
steps.instructions: Before any code, write your chart out as pseudocode comments at the top of the file. One instruction per line, indented to show what is inside the decision.

steps.title: Declare the inputs
steps.instructions: The printer-credit rule needs the pages the student wants to print and the credit they have left. Declare pagesRequested and creditRemaining with descriptive names and sensible values.

steps.title: Write the decision
hints: The condition goes in the round brackets: pagesRequested <= creditRemaining
Each branch needs its own console.log
The word else has no condition of its own - it is everything the first case was not

steps.title: Confirm the code matches the plan
steps.instructions: Read your pseudocode comments and your code side by side. Every shape on your chart should appear once in the code, in the same order. Then change the values so the other branch runs, and check that it does.

requirements.title: pagesRequested is declared
requirements.description: A descriptive variable holds how many pages were asked for

requirements.title: creditRemaining is declared
requirements.description: A descriptive variable holds the credit left

requirements.title: The decision compares the two
requirements.description: An if statement compares pagesRequested against creditRemaining

requirements.title: Both branches exist
requirements.description: An else branch is present, matching the diamond's second exit

requirements.title: Both branches print
requirements.description: Two or more console.log calls, so each path reports an outcome
